reasons: The tests were read, not run, so passing status is not confirmed.
Several tests match exact error wording.

terms.meaning: the most independent action a process is allowed to take, from fully autonomous down to human only
the strictest ceiling set by any constraint, which is the one that applies
a number giving the strictness order of a ceiling, where a higher number means stricter
an external rule, such as a regulation or contract, that limits what a process may do

used_by: the pytest run for the schema tests

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Imports pytest, the validation error type and the feasibility types from the schema package.
sections.why: The tests need these types to build and check feasibility records.

sections.name: constraint
sections.title: Building a constraint
sections.what: Builds a regulatory constraint with a sample instrument, jurisdiction, requirement, ceiling and step, and lets tests change the kind or ceiling.
sections.why: Most constraint tests start from this sample.
sections.watch_out: The sample instrument and jurisdiction are fixed values that tests rely on implicitly.

sections.name: readiness
sections.title: Building data readiness
sections.what: Builds a readiness record with required, available, governed and missing datasets, using sample values.
sections.why: Shared starting point for the readiness tests.
sections.watch_out: Governed datasets must be a subset of available ones, so changing one list may cause an error.

sections.name: assessment
sections.title: Building an assessment
sections.what: Builds a feasibility assessment from a list of constraints, setting the binding ceiling to the strictest of them. If no list is given, it uses one sample constraint.
sections.why: The binding ceiling is calculated, not chosen, so the helper calculates it the same way.
sections.watch_out: Passing an empty list gives an assessment with no constraints, while passing nothing uses the sample constraint. These two cases must not be confused.

sections.name: TestAutonomyCeilingOrdering
sections.title: Ordering of autonomy ceilings
sections.what: Checks that ceilings run from most to least permissive, that the strictest of a set is the least permissive, that an empty set gives full autonomy, and that the ordering is by severity rather than by text.
sections.why: Alphabetical ordering of the names would give wrong answers, so the test documents why severity exists.
sections.watch_out: Overriding the less-than comparison would change how these values sort as text everywhere they are used.

sections.name: TestBindingCeilingIsComputed
sections.title: Binding ceiling is computed
sections.what: Checks that the binding ceiling comes from the constraints, that a more permissive ceiling beside a stricter constraint is refused, that no constraints means full autonomy, and that blocking constraints are listed.
sections.why: Autonomy must never be proposed where a regulator bars it, and the refusal exists to prevent that.
sections.watch_out: The refusal test matches exact phrases in the error message.

sections.name: TestConstraint
sections.title: Constraint rules
sections.what: Checks that the constraint kinds form a closed list, that an unknown kind is refused, that instrument, jurisdiction and requirement must each be filled in, and that the evidence list must be given.
sections.why: A bare statement such as regulatory requirements apply is not a usable constraint.

sections.name: TestDataReadiness
sections.title: Data readiness rules
sections.what: Checks the readiness ratio, that available datasets must be among the required ones, that governed datasets must be among the available ones, that nothing required means fully ready, and that available but ungoverned data does not count as ready.
sections.why: Data that cannot be governed is not usable at decision time, so it must not count toward readiness.
sections.watch_out: The ratio is calculated, so changing how ready is counted changes every readiness score.

sections.name: TestBoundary
sections.title: Assessment carries no scoring or value fields
sections.what: Checks that the assessment and the constraint have no scorecard field and no cost, savings, or similar value fields.
sections.why: The docstring says the assessor informs the scorecard but does not set it, so it must not carry scores or money figures.
sections.watch_out: Adding a banned field name to either model will fail this test on purpose.

summary: Tests the feasibility rules: which autonomy ceiling applies, which constraints bind, and how data readiness is measured.
purpose: Makes sure the strictest applicable autonomy limit is always the one recorded, and that data readiness and constraints are described completely.
why: The module docstring says the binding ceiling is computed, never asserted. Stating a permissive ceiling beside a stricter constraint would allow autonomy a regulator has barred.
how: Builds sample constraints, readiness records and assessments. Then checks the ordering of ceilings, that the binding ceiling is computed from the constraints, that constraints are fully described, that readiness rules hold, and that the assessment carries no value or scoring fields.
inputs: Sample values built inside the file, using the package's feasibility types.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. No files are written.
risks: The ordering test depends on severity numbers. Changing a ceiling's severity changes which one counts as strictest everywhere.
debug: If an assessment is refused, read the message, since it names the constraint that set the ceiling. If the ordering test fails, check the severity values on the ceiling type.
